title: How to Turn Scanned Pages into a Searchable PDF
description: Learn the difference between image-only scans and OCR text layers, how to prepare pages and how to verify searchable PDF output.
intro: A scanned PDF may look like a document while containing only page images. Optical character recognition (OCR) can add a text layer that makes words searchable, but recognition quality depends on scan quality and language support.

sections.heading: Image-only scan or searchable document?
paragraphs: If you cannot select or search words in a scan, its pages may be stored as images. OCR analyses those images and attempts to recognize characters, adding text that a PDF reader can search.
OCR is not a guarantee of perfect transcription. Handwriting, low contrast, skewed pages, unusual fonts and complex tables can reduce accuracy.

sections.heading: Prepare a clear source
paragraphs: Use a readable scan with straight pages, good contrast and enough resolution to distinguish characters. Remove unnecessary borders and verify page orientation before recognition.
For a large document, test a representative page first. Check names, numbers, punctuation, columns and any text that will be used for decisions.

sections.heading: Run OCR and review the result
paragraphs: Use Make PDF Searchable to add a searchable text layer to supported scans. Then search for several known words and compare recognized text with the source page.
If you need to extract images or convert pages to pictures instead, use PDF to JPG. Keep the original scan: OCR output can require manual correction, especially for important records.

faq.question: Does OCR change the page image?
faq.answer: OCR typically adds a text layer over or alongside the scanned page image, but inspect the result to understand the tool's output.

faq.question: Is OCR always accurate?
faq.answer: No. Accuracy depends on scan quality, font, language and layout. Proofread names, figures and critical passages.

faq.question: Can OCR recognize handwriting?
faq.answer: Handwriting recognition varies considerably and may not be supported. Treat any recognized handwriting as a draft requiring careful review.

faq.question: Can I search a PDF after OCR?
faq.answer: A successful OCR text layer generally enables search, but test known terms in your PDF reader after processing.
